title: Vertical Stabilizer Front Spar Attachment Land — Corrosion Removal and Restoration
abstract: Permanent repair for corrosion at the vertical stabilizer front spar attachment land, giving the removal limits, the restoration sequence and the ultrasonic check of the attachment bolt holes.

sections.purpose: To give the permanent repair for corrosion found at the vertical stabilizer front spar attachment land, and the limits within which material removal alone restores the structure.
sections.damage_assessment: Corrosion at this land is caused by moisture tracking down the fin leading edge and collecting at the attachment fitting where the drainage is poor. It is found at the scheduled attachment inspection with the fairing removed. Assess the damage after removing the protective finish over the whole land, not only over the visible product, because the corrosion follows the faying face inward. Measure the depth of the deepest pit after a light clean-up and record the distance to the nearest attachment bolt hole. Any corrosion product inside an attachment bolt hole takes the finding outside this scheme immediately and must be referred to the engineering department. Confirm the drainage condition at the same visit; a blocked drain path returns the damage inside two years whatever the repair does.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the fin root fairing and get access to the attachment land. Remove the protective finish over the whole land and for 60 mm beyond. Clean the area and examine it under magnification. Remove the corrosion product with a non-metallic abrasive and blend the pits to a 20 to 1 ratio, keeping the removal within the limits below. Measure the remaining thickness at five points across the land and record each value. Do the ultrasonic inspection of every attachment bolt hole in the group and record the traces. Where a hole shows an indication, stop and refer the finding. Clean the land with the approved solvent. Apply the two-stage surface treatment within the application window. Install the strap D5530114423837 across the blended area where the drawing requires it, wet with sealant, and fasten it with the bolts EN241099-8D. Install the clip D5530116876335 at the drain position and confirm that the drain path is clear with a water flow test. Apply the sealing bead along the land edge and tool it so that water is carried to the drain rather than held at the joint. Re-apply the paint scheme and install the fairing.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an ultrasonic inspection of every attachment bolt hole at completion and keep the traces as the baseline. Repeat the detailed visual inspection of the land at every heavy check and the ultrasonic inspection of the bolt holes at every second heavy check. Confirm the drain path at every inspection. New corrosion at a repaired land within three years requires the drainage to be re-assessed rather than the land to be blended again.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Material removal up to 6 per cent of the local land thickness over an area not exceeding 3 000 square millimetres, with no removal within 25 mm of an attachment bolt hole and no corrosion product inside any bolt hole.

repair_drawings.title: Blend envelope, restoration strap and drain reinstatement, fin front spar attachment land

type_data.fastener_pattern: One row of 14 tension bolts at 26 mm pitch with 22 mm edge distance, clear of every attachment bolt hole by at least 25 mm.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit is attached provided the removal is inside the limits and the drain path is proven clear. New corrosion within three years requires the drainage to be re-assessed before any further blending.
